item.title: Toddler's tragic death sparks manslaughter charges after alleged poisoning
item.description: Police say the toddler's lips turned blue and she suffered a seizure after ingesting kratom pills, but neither adult called 911 or sought medical care.
item.content:encoded:
A Florida father and the mother of his children are behind bars after police said they failed to seek emergency care when a 2-year-old girl turned blue, suffered a seizure and began breathing abnormally after allegedly ingesting kratom pills.

Jerome Jonathon Jordan, 35, and Charlene Rea O'Connell, 32, are each charged with aggravated manslaughter of a child and child neglect causing great bodily harm in the death of 2-year-old Jonnie Jordan, according to the West Melbourne Police Department.

The charges come more than two months after Jonnie was rushed to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne on May 18. 

Hospital staff pronounced the toddler dead shortly after she arrived.

STEPDAD ACCUSED OF SEX ASSAULT AS COPS WIDEN PROBE INTO GIRL’S LETHAL BENADRYL INGREDIENT DOSE

Investigators said the tragedy unfolded the night before at O'Connell's Palm Bay home, where Jonnie allegedly got into kratom pills belonging to Jordan and O'Connell.

Police said they believe the toddler consumed as many as two-and-a-half pills before both adults realized what had happened.

According to investigators, Jordan and O'Connell watched as Jonnie's lips turned blue, she suffered a seizure and began breathing abnormally. But instead of calling 911 or taking the little girl to a hospital, police allege they failed to seek medical care.

DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED

Authorities said Jordan then drove Jonnie back to his sister's apartment in West Melbourne and put her to bed.

Hours later, after waking up and finding the toddler unresponsive, Jordan rushed her to the hospital, where doctors pronounced her dead.

Investigators said Jordan initially urged hospital staff to administer Narcan, leading detectives to suspect an overdose early in the investigation.

SHARON STONE'S TERRIFYING WEED WITHDRAWAL SPARKS WARNING ABOUT TODAY'S POTENT MARIJUANA

The Brevard County  Medical Examiner's Office determined that Jonnie died of acute mitragynine intoxication, according to police.

According to the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, part of the National Institutes of Health, kratom is a herbal substance made from the leaves of a tropical tree native to Southeast Asia and is commonly sold in powders, capsules, gummies and drinks.

Some people use it for its stimulant or pain-relieving effects, though federal health officials have repeatedly warned about its safety.

While kratom remains legal under federal law, the Drug Enforcement Administration announced earlier this month it had begun the process of temporarily placing high-potency 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products and certain related synthetic compounds into Schedule I, citing their high potential for abuse and opioid-like effects. The action does not apply to natural kratom leaf products.

Following the medical examiner's findings and a months-long investigation, police arrested Jordan and O'Connell on Thursday. Both are being held without bond at the Brevard County Jail.

Police said Jordan's sister, whose apartment Jonnie was taken to after leaving O'Connell's home, is not facing any charges.

item.title: Indiana's Curt Cignetti roasts the SEC as ESPN starts their promotional campaign already: 'we don't whine'
item.description: Curt Cignetti fired back at SEC coaches and Greg Sankey at Big Ten media days, calling out the hype machine around strength of schedule excuses.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 college football season hasn't even started, and the war of words and messaging is already ramping up.

The SEC this year moves to nine conference games, a large shift that will necessarily impact win-loss records and takes away one of their biggest advantages over the Big Ten or other nine-game conferences. As a result, at SEC media days recently, several coaches and even conference commissioner Greg Sankey started their promotional and excuse campaign for the College Football Playoff.

Despite not reaching the National Championship game for three straight seasons and going 2-7 in the playoff against other Power 4 conference teams, the SEC has started their campaign by saying that they deserve more teams in the tournament. Why? Because of their depth and strength of schedule.

SEC WANTS MORE PLAYOFF FAVORITISM AS GREG SANKEY COMPLAINS ABOUT 'UNSATISFACTORY' TALKS WITH CFB PLAYOFF

Sure, depth and strength of schedule matters, but winning your games matters too. And that's where the SEC coaches and Sankey are going through a bit of a contradictory crisis.

When the SEC was dominant, winning title after title, the narrative went that the depth meant that their teams were battle hardened by playoff time. Other conferences didn't progress through the regular season gauntlet of SEC teams, making them less prepared at the end of the year.

Now that the SEC has fallen behind the Big Ten and are moving to nine conference games, the narrative-building has changed. Just listen to ESPN's Laura Rutledge make excuses for a season and schedule that hasn't happened yet.

LANE KIFFIN MAKES RIDICULOUS EXCUSES FOR SEC'S POOR RECENT PERFORMANCE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

"So, I think one of the reasons why the SEC may not have advanced as far in the playoffs as some SEC fans would like to see," Rutledge told Pat McAfee recently. "It's because the competition within the league is so difficult that nine games of craziness week in and week out are little different than other parts of other conferences. I'm not dissing on the Big 10.

"By the time they get to the end, there are not many left. For one, they eliminate each other, but furthermore, they're gassed. They're injured. They have issues. I'm not making excuses. I'm just pointing out facts because you were pointing out facts," she continued.

"I'm not making excuses," then makes excuses. Because ESPN is heavily invested in promoting the SEC, as their biggest media partners.

First, we have yet to see what a nine-game schedule does to the SEC. Second, implying that the previous eight-game schedule was just too much for these teams to handle is actually an argument against the strength of the conference. Third, what happened to the SEC being so battle hardened they could handle the rigors of a playoff run? Now they're just too tired.

Let's look at the 2024 Ohio State National Championship team as a counterpoint, shall we? The Buckeyes in 2024 had road games at Oregon, ranked No. 3 in the country at the time, and Penn State, which was also then ranked No. 3. It hosted No. 5 Indiana and finished with an always tough, physical, rivalry game against a solid Michigan team. It played three playoff teams in the regular season, including the No. 1 overall seed, Oregon, and another physical opponent in Iowa. All within seven weeks. Sounds pretty tough!

They then blew out a vaunted SEC team, Tennessee, 42-17, easily handled another top SEC team, Texas, and beat a very good Notre Dame team in the championship game. That's what good teams do. Indiana in 2025 played Ohio State to finish the season, then blew out Alabama, Oregon, and handled Miami to win a title. That's what good teams do.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Stop making excuses and win important games.

Speaking of excuses and Indiana, if there's one head coach who hates them more than anyone, it's Curt Cignetti. The defending champ took a very pointed shot at the SEC and the excuses culture they've created.

"I mean we don’t run a hype machine up here in the Midwest," Cignetti said on Thursday at Big Ten media days. "We believe everything’s earned, not given. And when we fall short, we say, ‘We fell short.’ We don’t cry a river, whine and complain. All right? And that’s why we’re the best."

Ouch.

Though, to be fair to the SEC, Notre Dame's in the Midwest and boy oh boy did they cry a river, whine, and complain after getting left out of the playoff last season.

He has a point though, about the current strategy around the SEC. For some reason, instead of saying, "hey, we believe we're the best, we'll go through whatever gauntlet we have in front of us, and beat people up in the playoff, because we're the best," they're saying "woe is us, it's just too tough to win games."

Maybe that's the reason the SEC has fallen behind, because they're consumed with talking about the difficult of playing road games at Mississippi State instead of Nebraska. Or Kentucky instead of Wisconsin. Maybe focus on winning, it's a guarantee the rest will take care of itself.

item.title: Chris Hemsworth shares terrifying footage from 'crazy' plane ride through lightning and severe turbulence
item.description: Video from Chris Hemsworth's Costa Rica family vacation captures a terrifying lightning storm mid-flight that he called a "crazy" moment.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Hemsworth's latest family vacation took a frightening turn when the actor found himself aboard a small plane caught in the middle of a lightning storm.

On Wednesday, the "Thor" star, 42, captured the Costa Rica family trip with wife Elsa Pataky and their three children in a YouTube vlog, including a "life-threatening" plane ride. 

Footage from the trip captured lightning flashing around the aircraft as turbulence shook the cabin. Hemsworth's unease was evident in the clip, as he could be seen mouthing, "What the f—?"

In the caption of the video, Hemsworth also called it a "crazy plane ride."

CHRIS HEMSWORTH SHUTS DOWN CLAIMS ALZHEIMER'S FEARS FORCED HIM TO QUIT HOLLYWOOD: 'REALLY... P---ED ME OFF'

Fortunately, the flight landed safely, and the scare didn't stop the Hemsworth family from making the most of the vacation.

The action-packed trip featured everything from surfing and ATV riding to cliff jumping, fishing and hiking through waterfalls. At one point, Pataky playfully shoved her husband into a waterfall.

CHRIS HEMSWORTH, BRAD PITT, BEN AFFLECK ARE AMONG MALE STARS GETTING BETTER WITH AGE: PHOTOS

The couple, who married in 2010, share daughter India and twin sons Sasha and Tristan. The family has long embraced an adventurous lifestyle, frequently sharing glimpses of outdoor excursions from their home in Australia and while traveling abroad.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The vacation scare comes several years after Hemsworth publicly revealed he was rethinking how he approached work and family following a health revelation during filming of National Geographic's "Limitless."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

While undergoing genetic testing for the series, the actor learned he carries two copies of the APOE4 gene, which is linked to an increased risk of developing Alzheimer's disease later in life.

Shortly after the news was made public in 2022, he took a break from acting. Together, the two bits of news led to rumors that he was retiring, or that he'd already developed the disease, which he said was very upsetting to hear.

"It really kind of p---ed me off because it felt like I had been vulnerable with something personal and shared this," he admitted in an interview with Vanity Fair in 2024.

"No matter how much I said, ‘This is not a death sentence,’ the story became that I have dementia and I’m reconsidering life and retiring and so on."

He then joked, "I did read a really funny comment at the bottom of one article: ‘I hope Chris forgets he’s retiring and comes back.’"

Fox News Digital's Emily Trainham contributed to this post.

item.title: NFL legend Rob Gronkowski has simple advice for Caitlin Clark: 'Keep shutting up the haters'
item.description: NFL legend Rob Gronkowski has high praise and simple advice for Caitlin Clark as the discourse around the Indiana Fever star has continued to rage on.
item.content:encoded:
NFL legend Rob Gronkowski has high praise and some simple advice for Caitlin Clark: "Keep shutting up the haters" with her play.

Amid the rampant discourse about Clark that has dominated the internet, Gronkowski told Fox News Digital in a recent interview that she’s doing a "great job" of handling it all.

"She's doing a great job handling herself. She really is. I'm not in her shoes. I'm not in her situation. If I was, though, I would kind of handle it very similar to how she's handling it. She really is doing a great job," Gronkowski told Fox News Digital in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I would just say one piece of advice, keep balling because if you keep balling, you're going to keep shutting up the haters."

The Indiana Fever have won their last four games, and Clark has been great, averaging just over 30 points per game during that winning streak. While Clark has been good, so have her teammates, as Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston have both been key contributors.

Gronkowski praised Clark’s teammates for supporting her throughout the season.

"What I do appreciate, what she's going to need to help with is her teammates. That's who's going to lift you up. If you've got your teammates protecting you, that says a lot right there. It really does. And she does. Her team does pick her up. They protect her as well, and that's huge," Gronkowski told Fox News Digital on behalf of eBay.

NFL LEGEND ROB GRONKOWSKI DETAILS TRAVIS KELCE AND TAYLOR SWIFT'S 'MAGNIFICENT' WEDDING

"That says a lot about your personality and about who you are throughout the season, how you practice, how you prepare, is that if your teammates are behind you, you know that doing the right things."

Gronkowski said Clark will truly be the face of the WNBA once the league steps in and does something about the hard fouls she has received, in addition to winning something significant.

"I think she's going to be the face eventually, like truly where the WNBA steps in and they're like, ‘Okay, like enough of all this wishwashing that's going on with her and the punishment that that she's taking out on the basketball court. Let's truly make her to face the league. I think I would say it once she keeps balling out and also wins something pretty significant," Gronkowski said.

The New England Patriots legend said he isn’t a diehard fan and is more of a casual fan of the WNBA. He talked about how in the NFL and NBA, you don’t become the face of the league until you have about "four or five years under their belt."

Gronkowski, a four-time Super Bowl champion, is one of the greatest tight ends of all time. He spent nine seasons with the Patriots before retiring in 2019. He came out of retirement in 2020 and played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Tom Brady for two seasons before retiring again.

In 11 seasons, the five-time Pro Bowler caught 621 receptions for 9,286 yards and 92 touchdowns.

Clark and the Fever will look to keep it rolling when they play the Portland Fire on Friday at 10 p.m. ET.

item.title: Washington school district reviewing incident of employee making celebratory remark about Charlie Kirk's death
item.description: The Lake Washington School District says it launched a review after viral video captured a staff member apparently celebrating Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.content:encoded:
A Washington school district says it has launched a review after a woman identified online as a high school nurse appeared in a confrontation that went viral this week about Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk, during which she was heard saying, "Thank God he's dead."

The Lake Washington School District confirmed to Fox News Digital on Wednesday that it is aware of the video circulating on social media involving a district employee and said it is reviewing the circumstances while emphasizing that the views expressed do not reflect those of the district.

"Lake Washington School District (LWSD) is aware of a video circulating on social media involving a district staff member," a spokesperson for the school district told Fox News Digital in a statement Wednesday. 

"We have received concerns from community members regarding the statements and conduct shown in the video."

OKLAHOMA STATE AGENCY FIRES STAFF ATTORNEY AFTER ANTI-ICE SOCIAL MEDIA TIRADE

In the video shared on X by the account Right Angle News Network, a woman identified in the post as a nurse at Eastlake High School named Kelsey Ballin is heard saying, "Oh my God, thank God he’s dead, bye," after someone else references Charlie Kirk.

She also appears to mockingly blow a kiss, stick out her tongue, and then give the finger in the incident, which reportedly took place at a farmer's market. Other people in the video were wearing Kirk "Freedom" t-shirts during the incident.

Kirk was assassinated on Sept. 10 while speaking at Utah Valley University during his "American Comeback Tour."

UTAH VALLEY UNIVERSITY SCRAPS CONTROVERSIAL COMMENCEMENT SPEAKER WHO CRITICIZED CHARLIE KIRK AFTER HIS MURDER

Eastlake High School is part of the Lake Washington School District, located in Sammamish, Washington, and serves grades 9 through 12.

"The district takes these concerns seriously," the spokesperson continued. "While we cannot comment on individual personnel matters, district leadership has initiated a review of the circumstances surrounding this incident and will follow established processes as the review moves forward. It is important to note the views expressed in the video do not reflect the values or positions of Lake Washington School District."

The spokesperson went on to say that, "LWSD is committed to providing welcoming, safe and inclusive learning environments for all students, families, staff and community members. We expect all employees to uphold the professional standards and the values of the district and to contribute to a culture of respect, dignity and civil discourse."

WISCONSIN TEACHER FIRED AFTER SOCIAL MEDIA POST ADVOCATING TO 'MAKE AMERICANS GREAT ASSASSINS AGAIN'

"At the same time," the spokesperson added, "District employees retain rights and protections as private citizens. Balancing these principles is central to how the district approaches situations like this one. Because this is an ongoing personnel matter, we are unable to provide additional information at this time. We remain committed to our values as an organization for developing students that are prepared as members of a diverse community."

When asked about its policies governing employees' conduct outside of work and on social media, the district referred Fox News Digital to its staff conduct policy, as well as separate guidance addressing employees' use of social media.

Fox News Digital reached out to Turning Point USA for comment, and was referred to a an X post Thursday from Andrew Kolvet, spokesman for TPUSA, where he reshared the X post from Right Angle News Network and wrote, "Why are so many of these awful humans drawn to children, schools, and medicine?"

Fox News Digital reached out to Ballin for comment.

item.title: Fox News Poll: GOP divisions shape Texas Senate race
item.description: Ken Paxton trails James Talarico by three points in the Texas Senate race as character concerns and a GOP unity gap reshape the 2026 midterm battle.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump won the Lone Star state by nearly 14 percentage points in 2024, but a new Fox News Poll of Texas registered voters suggests this year's Senate race is far less settled. Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton has yet to fully unify the GOP despite the president’s endorsement in the GOP primary against incumbent Sen. John Cornyn.

In addition, more voters are concerned Paxton lacks the character to serve than worry Democratic challenger James Talarico is too extreme, and more Democrats than Republicans are extremely motivated to vote (by 7 points) and extremely interested in the midterms (by 6).

Those dynamics give Talarico a 3-point edge over Paxton (51% vs. 48%) in the Senate contest (within the survey’s margin of sampling error).

Talarico's advantage in the race grows to 6 points among both extremely motivated and extremely interested voters (53% vs. 47% in each group).

FOX NEWS POLL: DEMOCRATIC ENTHUSIASM SHAPES NORTH CAROLINA SENATE RACE

Most independents (68%) and virtually all Democrats support Talarico (98%), while fewer Republicans are unified behind Paxton (89%).

In part, that’s because one quarter of non-MAGA Republicans back Talarico (24%).

Paxton is the choice among White evangelical Christians, White men without a college degree, rural voters, regular worship attenders, men and voters ages 65 and older.

Some of Talarico’s best groups are Black voters, moderates, voters under age 30, Hispanic voters, women and voters with a college degree.

"Although Paxton dominated Cornyn in the GOP primary, that bruising contest left scars," said Republican pollster Daron Shaw, who conducts Fox News polls with Democrat Chris Anderson. 

"He has considerable work to do with non-MAGA Republicans and independents, and that undoubtedly requires aggressively tying Talarico to the Democratic Party’s far left." 

By a 12-point margin, more voters are concerned Paxton lacks the character to serve as a senator than believe Talarico is too extreme (59% vs. 47%).

Twice as many Republicans are concerned about Paxton's character as Democrats are that Talarico is too extreme (36% vs. 17%).

FOX NEWS POLL: COOL YOUR SERVERS! VOTERS REJECT DATA CENTERS

Still, about 8 in 10 Paxton and Talarico supporters say their backing is more about where the candidates stand on the issues than who they are as people. 

Trump received a 55% favorable vs. 44% unfavorable rating in the 2024 Texas Fox News Voter Analysis (FNVA) election survey. Today, those numbers have flipped: 45% favorable vs. 54% unfavorable, for a minus-9 net negative rating.

Paxton garners a minus-6 net personal rating, 45% favorable vs. 51% unfavorable, while Talarico is in positive territory by 6 points, 49% vs. 43%.

Talarico is more popular than the Democratic Party while the GOP edges out Paxton. 

While both parties are viewed negatively, the GOP is underwater by only 2 points (48% favorable vs. 50% unfavorable), compared with the Democratic Party at minus-9 (45% vs. 54%).

Despite Texas being a border state, nearly 4 in 10 say inflation will be the most important issue to their Senate vote, while 2 in 10 say immigration and 1 in 10 say healthcare, political divisions and unemployment.

By more than a 2-to-1 margin, Texas voters say they are falling behind financially rather than getting ahead (35% vs. 16%). Half are holding steady.

In the race for governor, incumbent Republican Gov. Greg Abbott is favored by 1 point over Democrat Gina Hinojosa.

Part of Abbott's edge comes from a touch more crossover support: 12% of Talarico supporters back Abbott, while 9% of Paxton supporters back Hinojosa.

Hinojosa has the advantage among extremely motivated (+6) and extremely interested voters (+5).

Abbott has a net positive personal rating by a single point (50% favorable vs. 49% unfavorable). Hinojosa is in positive territory by 11 points (45% vs. 34%), although nearly 1 in 5 are unable to rate her.

Texas last elected a Democratic governor in 1990 (Ann Richards), a Democratic Senator in 1988 (Lloyd Bentsen), and a Democratic presidential candidate in 1976 (Jimmy Carter).

A closer look at the Hispanic electorate

Hispanic voters say their Senate pick will be driven by inflation, as roughly 4 in 10 say it will be the most important issue to their vote and another 4 in 10 say they’re falling behind financially. This mostly matches views among all Texas voters.

And as is the case with voters overall, there is an enthusiasm gap, as more Hispanic Democrats than Hispanic Republicans are interested and motivated to vote in the midterms.

Overall, Hispanic voters prefer Talarico by 18 points (59% vs. 41%).

Some 9% of Hispanic GOP voters crossover to support Talarico while 5% of Hispanic Democrats favor Paxton.

CLICK HERE FOR CROSSTABS AND TOPLINE

In 2024, Trump topped former Vice President Kamala Harris among Hispanic voters in Texas by 1 point, according to the Texas FNVA survey (49% Harris vs. 50% Trump).

By 20 points, more Hispanic voters are concerned that Paxton lacks the character to serve as senator than feel Talarico is too extreme (61% concerned vs. 41%).

For the governor’s race, Hispanic voters back Hinojosa by 16 points in the new survey. By comparison, they preferred Beto O’Rourke over Abbott by 14 points in 2022.

More than half of Hispanic voters view Talarico (57% favorable), Hinojosa (53%), and the Democratic Party (53%) positively, while more than half have negative views of Paxton (56% unfavorable), Abbott (56%), Trump (61%), and the Republican Party (59%).

Conducted July 23-27, 2026, under the direction of Beacon Research (D) and Shaw & Company Research (R), this Fox News survey includes interviews with a sample of 1,006 Texas registered voters randomly selected from a statewide voter file. Respondents spoke with live interviewers on landlines (72) and cellphones (681) or completed the survey online after receiving a text (253). Results based on the full sample have a margin of sampling error of ±3 percentage points. 

The survey includes an oversample of 296 Hispanic voters, bringing the sample size for that subgroup to 556 (±4). Sampling error for results among subgroups is higher. In addition to sampling errors, question wording and order can influence results. Weights are generally applied to age, race, education and area variables to ensure the demographics are representative of the registered voter population. Sources for developing weight targets include the most recent American Community Survey, Fox News Voter Analysis and voter file data.

item.title: Pentagon fires back after Mark Kelly accuses Pete Hegseth of targeting women and Black military officers
item.description: The Department of War rejected Sen. Mark Kelly's claims that Pete Hegseth targeted women and Black officers, citing merit-based promotion policies.
item.content:encoded:
The Department of War (DOW) rejected Sen. Mark Kelly's allegations Thursday that War Secretary Pete Hegseth targeted women and Black military officers because of their identities. 

In a statement to Fox News Digital responding to Kelly's interview on "Next Question with Katie Couric," the department pointed to statements from two Pentagon spokesmen maintaining that military promotions were based on merit, not race and gender.

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the department would not use a service member's identity when making promotion decisions.

SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES MERIT-BASED MILITARY PROMOTIONS, TARGETS BIDEN-ERA DEI POLICIES

"As we’ve said before, military promotions are given to those who have earned them. The Department will never consider the color of a service member’s skin or their gender as a factor in promotions," Parnell said in one of the statements cited by the department to Fox News Digital.

"Under President Trump and @SecWar Hegseth, meritocracy reigns supreme at the War Department."

"They also fire women, and they fire Black people because of their gender and the color of their skin," he told Couric. "They've done that repeatedly. They don't even try to make excuses about it. They just fire them."

Kelly, a retired Navy captain and member of the Armed Services Committee, previously accused Hegseth of removing former Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen. CQ Brown because of his race in an appearance Sunday on MS NOW's "PoliticsNation." President Donald Trump fired Brown shortly after taking office again in 2025.

The Arizona Democrat also pointed to the removal of Adm. Lisa Franchetti, the first woman to serve as chief of naval operations, accusing Hegseth of blocking promotions and removing officers because of their race or gender. Kelly said the personnel changes would deprive the military of experienced leaders.

HEGSETH SAYS PENTAGON WILL REVIEW MARK KELLY'S PUBLIC STATEMENTS ABOUT CLASSIFIED BRIEFING AMID ONGOING FEUD

"We’re losing a generation of leaders because there will be women and Black people that’ll say, ‘Well, I don’t feel like I have opportunity here anymore. I’m just going to leave mid-career instead of staying.’ So, we’ll lose some of our best people," Kelly told Couric. 

Acting Pentagon press secretary Joel Valdez also rejected the premise that the department's personnel decisions were discriminatory. The DOW directed Fox News Digital to his statement as part of its response to Kelly's allegations.

"Here’s the bottom line: anyone who has an issue with merit-based promotions should reconsider their values. Promotions based solely on race and gender is wrong," Valdez said on X last month.

AIR FORCE RESCINDING 135 PROMOTIONS AFTER TEST SCORING ERROR: 'THIS IS GOING TO BE HARD'

Trump dismissed Brown in February 2025 and selected retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Dan "Razin" Caine to replace him. 

Hegseth separately requested nominees to replace Franchetti, Air Force Vice Chair of Staff Gen. Jim Slide and the judge advocate general of the Army, Navy and Air Force during a broader Pentagon leadership shake-up.

Military officials questioned whether women and minority officers had been singled out because of their identities, an allegation Pentagon officials strongly disputed. The department did not publicly disclose its specific rationale for the removals.

Hegseth has maintained that promotions should be determined by performance rather than identity. During a September address to senior military leaders at Marine Corps Base Quantico, Virginia, he described identity-based advancement as a form of poor leadership.

"Real toxic leadership is promoting people based on immutable characteristics or quotas instead of based on merit," Hegseth said.

Fox News Digital's Michael Lee contributed to this report.

item.title: Former Auburn two-way star Bobby Hunt, Chiefs Super Bowl I starter, dead at 85
item.description: Bobby Hunt led the AFL with 10 interceptions the year he started at safety for the Kansas City Chiefs in their Super Bowl I loss to Green Bay.
item.content:encoded:
Bobby Hunt, a former do-it-all football standout for the Auburn Tigers, has died. He was 85.

The Alabama Sports Hall of Fame, which inducted Hunt in 2015, confirmed his death. "Our thoughts and prayers are with his family and friends," the hall wrote in a tribute shared to Facebook.

Details on Hunt's cause of death were not immediately made public.

At Lanett High School in Alabama, Hunt played quarterback and defensive back. He also spent time at both the punter and punt returner positions.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

He took that all-around talent to Auburn, where he continued to play quarterback and safety.

Hunt was coached by Ralph "Shug" Jordan at Auburn. According to AL.com, Hunt's talent was noticed by Auburn's top rival. Famed former Alabama coach Paul "Bear" Bryant once described Hunt as "just a great football player — that’s all."

After his two-way college football career, Hunt was picked by the Dallas Texans in the 11th round of the 1962 American Football League draft.

Once he reached the professional ranks, Hunt focused strictly on safety. He recorded eight interceptions as a rookie and earned first-team All-AFL honors before the Texans relocated to Kansas City, Missouri, in 1963 and became the Chiefs.

Three seasons later, Hunt was in the starting lineup when the Chiefs faced the Green Bay Packers in the first Super Bowl.

Hunt finished his professional football career with a two-season stint with the expansion Cincinnati Bengals.

Hunt appeared in 112 games as a pro, finishing his career with 42 interceptions. After his playing days ended, Hunt joined the coaching ranks as an assistant with the Buffalo Bills.

item.title: WNBA faces growing Sophie Cunningham movement as new rallies are set for Fever games in Oregon, Minnesota
item.description: Rallies supporting Sophie Cunningham are planned outside WNBA arenas in Portland and Minneapolis after a chaotic Seattle game sparked national debate.
item.content:encoded:
"Sophie Night" is coming to Democratic strongholds this weekend.

Upcoming WNBA games in Portland, Oregon, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, will feature rallies outside the arenas in support of Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham — the fan-favorite teammate of Caitlin Clark who has spoken out in defense of women’s sports.

A rally in Portland will be led by Washington-based activist Amy Sousa, who helped organize the Cunningham rally outside Seattle’s Climate Pledge Arena on Tuesday. A second rally in Minneapolis will be led by XX-XY Athletics founder and former U.S. gymnastics national champion Jennifer Sey.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY ROCKS WNBA GAME AS 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' ACTIVISTS FACE COUNTERPROTEST

Sousa said organizers already had a smaller Portland gathering in mind but were unsure whether they would publicize it. The national controversy that erupted after the Seattle game convinced them to make it bigger and louder.

"We were just going to do something quiet with just a couple of us, and seeing what happened to those girls, we just thought, ‘We can’t be quiet,’" Sousa told Fox News Digital.

The Portland rally is scheduled for 5:30 p.m. Friday outside the Moda Center before the Fever face the Portland Fire at 7 p.m. local time. The Minneapolis rally will take place ahead of Indiana’s noon game against the Minnesota Lynx at Target Center on Sunday.

STORM CO-OWNER SUSPENDED AFTER INCIDENT WITH SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FANS AS STAR BREAKS SILENCE ON CONTROVERSY

"I don’t want to be quiet about this," Sousa said. "I want to stand in public solidarity with those girls. I also want to stand in public solidarity with Sophie and keep this momentum going."

The events follow a chaotic night in Seattle that transformed Cunningham’s position on transgender athletes into a national flashpoint.

Supporters gathered outside Climate Pledge Arena before Tuesday’s Fever-Storm game to thank Cunningham for saying girls should not have to compete against biological males or share locker rooms with them. Counterprotesters carrying signs in support of transgender inclusion assembled nearby.

Sousa described the gathering outside the arena as overwhelmingly positive. The atmosphere changed after some of the Cunningham supporters entered the game.

Two 16-year-old girls wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts sat courtside and held a sign reading, "Thank you Sophie for speaking up for girls." The teenagers alleged that Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton approached them, cursed at them and called them "f---ing insane."

The girls said Keaton also invoked religion, telling them that she hoped Jesus could forgive them for their alleged sin and that "God can save you." One of the girls was left sobbing at halftime.

One of the girls had previously experienced facing a trans athlete in the past, Sousa said.

Sousa added the girl’s courtside ticket should have provided a rare opportunity to celebrate a professional athlete who supported her cause.

"It’s a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for many people to have courtside tickets," Sousa said. "When else in her life necessarily is she going to have an opportunity to sit courtside? She should have just been having the time of her life, and instead, she was reduced to tears."

Journalist Brandi Kruse, who attended the game and helped chaperone the teenagers, told Fox News Digital that she also saw unidentified Storm players direct thumbs-down gestures toward girls in the group. Cunningham was loudly booed by portions of the crowd whenever she touched the ball.

The controversy generated a swift response from the Storm and the league.

"We are aware one of our co-owners made comments to two fans in attendance at last night’s game," Storm majority owner Ginny Gilder said. "We apologize that this happened. Everyone who attends a Storm game deserves to feel welcome, and we remain committed to creating an inclusive environment where every fan is treated with respect."

The WNBA subsequently fined Keaton an undisclosed amount and barred her from attending the Storm’s next five home games. The Storm said it respected the league’s punishment and remained committed to providing "a welcoming and respectful environment" for fans.

Cunningham also responded to the girls’ account and promised to send them gifts.

"I truly believe there is a safe space and love for EVERYBODY," Cunningham wrote on X. "Biological girls, biological boys, trans women, and trans men. Everyone is welcome at my table! You can disagree and still be kind. Bravo to those girls for standing up for what they believe. You’ll be hearing from me soon💕 yay for gifts."

"Truly embarrassing of the co-owner," she added. "Unfortunately shows the type of leader she is."

Sousa said organizers expect a stronger counterprotest in Portland than the one they encountered in Seattle.

She has previously organized events in the city with the U.S. chapter of Women’s Declaration International. During one November 2023 event, WDI USA alleged that activists vandalized the event site, slashed vehicle tires and physically attacked women after the gathering moved onto a sidewalk.

Activist Kara Dansky, who attended that event, is traveling from Florida to participate in Friday’s rally, Sousa said.

"We absolutely expect opposition," Sousa said. "Hopefully, we’ll see things go a little differently, because I do think the cultural temperature is changing a little bit."

In Minneapolis, Sey’s involvement adds another connection to the Seattle controversy. The girls involved in the Keaton incident were wearing shirts produced by her company, which markets itself as an athletic brand committed to preserving female sports and spaces.

Sey, the 1986 U.S. women’s all-around gymnastics champion, recently told Fox News Digital that she had been trying to recruit Cunningham as an XX-XY Athletics ambassador after discovering that the WNBA player had privately praised one of the company’s advertisements.

"She’s the perfect person for us," Sey said at the time. "We have wanted to work with her for such a long time."

Cunningham drew support and backlash after telling ESPN that her position was not based on animosity toward transgender people.

"I think that I am here to extend love," Cunningham said. "But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

The guard later called the position "common sense" and said she would not retract it.

Sousa said the reaction to Seattle showed her that Cunningham’s supporters should continue making themselves visible.

"The public outrage at what happened to those girls is heartening, as it should be," Sousa said. "Now is the time to keep standing up and not keep it private, but do it loud, do it proud, and be there again as cheerleaders and in support of all women and girls."

item.title: President Trump pushes lawmakers on legislation as 'Protect College Sports Act' hangs on by a thread
item.description: Conference realignment caps, tampering penalties, and a $22.5 million retention pool were among the major sticking points in Senate negotiations.
item.content:encoded:
It was always going to be an uphill battle to pass the Protect College Sports Act, and now the process is at a crossroads that has gotten the attention of President Donald Trump.

Following negotiations that took place between multiple conferences around college athletics and senators Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) and others, we have officially reached a fork in the road.

There had been numerous phone calls between Big Ten commissioner Tony Petitti and SEC commissioner Greg Sankey over the last 24 hours related to their stance on the Protect College Sports Act, and whether or not each conference was prepared to put their support behind the legislation.

TICK TOCK: SEC AND BIG TEN RECEIVE REVISED PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT AS SENATE VOTE TIMELINE LOOMS

Now, as of Thursday evening, the mood has shifted in the nations capital as to whether this bill will ever make it to the Senate floor.

Earlier in the day, after OutKick-Fox News reached out for comment regarding their stance on the ongoing negotiations, a White House official had this to say about the legislation.

"The White House has been following these negotiations closely, and the President has been actively engaged. President Trump wants to save college sports, and he wants the bill done"

Clearly, Donald Trump wanted this legislation to make its way to his desk to be signed. But now, even with the potential for Senate Majority Leader John Thune to still bring cloture to a vote on Monday, which would allow the bill to be argued, there is dwindling optimism that anything of note will actually happen at this moment.

Essentially, all parties involved could not come to an agreement on certain language in the bill in time for vote.

"This is the legislation we need now. It will grant student-athletes unprecedented academic, health, and wellness benefits, rein in out-of-control agents, and stabilize transfer, eligibility, and revenue-sharing rules," NCAA President Charlie Baker said in a statement.

"While no bill is perfect, I implore college sports leaders and Senators to support this bill now. It is our best chance to deliver the benefits and level playing field student-athletes deserve while providing the protections institutions need to sustain college athletics long-term."

Obviously, things can change. But, the likelihood of that shrinks every day.

CONGRESS MAY FINALLY HAVE A BIPARTISAN PATH FORWARD ON COLLEGE ATHLETICS WITH CRUZ-CANTWELL LEGISLATION

The bipartisan bill was created to help navigate college athletics in this messy time, and out of courtrooms, with numerous eligibility lawsuits filed within the past week alone.

The back and forth between conference members, along with senators, centered around a number of different issues.

In their concessions to those within the SEC, Big Ten, ACC, Big 12, Notre Dame and Group of Six members, these were topics discussed over the past few days.

Obviously, with the clock ticking to get this legislation to the Senate floor, those in Washington were waiting on conferences to either put their support behind this or move on.

What we learned on Thursday was that it takes a lot longer than four weeks to come to an agreement on potential federal help.

Maybe, universities should just handle this on their own and stop asking Congress for help.

I guess we'll find out for certain over the next week, but the Protect College Sports Act is barely hanging on.

item.title: Trump Education Department probes school after teacher allegedly required same-sex students to kiss
item.description: The Trump administration opened a federal investigation into Denver Public Schools after a teacher allegedly required same-sex students to kiss in class.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration has opened a federal investigation into Denver Public Schools in response to allegations a high school teacher required students of the same sex to kiss as part of a classroom assignment, the Department of Education announced Tuesday.

"Schools have an obligation to prevent and address sexual assault," Kimberly Richey, assistant secretary for civil rights, said in a statement. "Yet in Colorado, school personnel are alleged to have compelled the sexual assault of minor students by forcing them to engage in blatantly sexualized conduct in class. 

"It is abhorrent and the Trump administration will fully investigate this perverse incident to protect students’ safety and vigorously uphold students’ rights across America."

The Education Department said it is investigating whether Denver Public Schools violated the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA), a federal law that gives parents the right to opt their children out of certain surveys, evaluations and instructional activities involving sensitive topics, including sexual behavior and attitudes.

COLORADO TEACHER FIRED AFTER STUDENTS ALLEGEDLY PRESSURED TO KISS CLASSMATES IN SKITS

The Department said it is "investigating incidents that took place at a Denver Public Schools high school involving a teacher who allegedly required students of the same sex to kiss each other in front of the classroom as part of a class assignment."

The Denver Public Schools board voted 7-0 May 20, CBS News reported, to consider the firing of French language and culture teacher Jennifer Honka at Northeast Early College for "incompetence and neglect of duty," finding she had at times allegedly suggested that students kiss during in-class skits.

An April 30 independent review, a copy of which was obtained by CBS Colorado, found that the students who were allegedly encouraged to kiss were always the same sex.

"One student told an NEC chemistry teacher about the skits in April 2024," CBS News reported. 

"The student was very uncomfortable and did not know what to do," the report said. "She went ahead and kissed another student at (Honka)'s direction. The student then shared a digital meme with (the chemistry teacher) that included a picture of (Honka) and the caption 'she makes girls kiss.' The meme had circulated among the students."

CBS News also reported that "one student interviewed directly in the independent review also testified that Honka always selected girls to act in the skits. Despite a nearly 50-50 split between boys and girls in the class, the student ‘could not recall Honka choosing a boy actor.’ This student refused to participate and testified that she received a zero score for a grade on this assignment."

TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS WOKE SCHOOLS ACCUSED OF HIDING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS

"Parents are entitled by law to be notified if their children will be surveyed or evaluated on sensitive information about sex behaviors or attitudes," the announcement from the Department of Education said. "SPPO will investigate whether parents were notified about this student evaluation and whether parent or student opt-outs or complaints were ignored. Additionally, OCR will investigate whether the district appropriately responded to the incident, consistent with the requirements of Title IX."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for Denver Public Schools said, "Denver Public Schools is reviewing the notice of directed investigation from OCR. It would be too early to comment on their assertions.

"The safety, emotional well-being and dignity of our students are the absolute highest priorities of DPS," the spokesperson continued. "Our actions to date have been wholly consistent with those priorities. Immediately after learning of student concerns with this teacher in March 2025, the district placed the teacher on administrative leave and completed a thorough investigation. 

"Based on the results of that investigation and an independent review by a state administrative law judge, the DPS Board of Education voted unanimously to terminate the employment of the teacher in May 2026.

"We deeply appreciate the bravery of the students who came forward and the staff who acted immediately as mandatory reporters," the spokesperson added. "We remain fully committed to holding personnel to the highest standards of conduct and ensuring a safe, supportive learning environment for all students."

WASHINGTON MOTHER PULLS CHILDREN FROM SCHOOL AFTER PRIDE LESSON SHOWN IN MUSIC CLASS WITHOUT NOTICE

The department announced a separate investigation into Washington state's Bethel School District over an LGBTQ Pride Month display that included vials labeled as testosterone.

In June, the school district said administrators discovered testosterone vials "that still contained a small amount of unknown liquid" included in a Pride Month display at Graham-Kapowsin High School and removed them after concluding the items had not been approved by school leadership.

They were subsequently removed.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Bethel School District said, "We are aware of the U.S. Department of Education investigation and will be cooperating in any way we can. In early June, district officials were made aware of a display at Graham-Kapowsin High School that included empty vials of testosterone as one of its visuals. The display also contained some vials that still contained a small amount of unknown liquid.

"The inclusion of the vials was entirely unauthorized and did not receive approval from school leadership or administration," the spokesperson continued. "Administrators immediately removed the vials and identified the individuals responsible for adding them without leadership approval. The vials were then turned over to the Pierce County Sheriff's Office.

"We are also actively reviewing our display oversight protocols to ensure all school materials strictly align with our educational standards and community expectations," the spokesperson added. "Our primary focus remains on maintaining a safe, respectful and focused learning environment for all of our students."

item.title: ABC accuses FCC of 'retaliation' as federal agency threatens to revoke Disney's broadcasting licenses
item.description: ABC accuses the FCC of retaliation over Jimmy Kimmel's jokes about President Trump, calling the early license renewal of eight Disney-owned stations punitive.
item.content:encoded:
ABC submitted a scathing filing to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Wednesday in opposition to petitions to deny its stations' license renewals.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr called the licenses of eight ABC-owned stations for early renewal in April. 

The Disney-owned ABC station's licenses were originally scheduled to be renewed between 2028 and 2031, but the FCC expedited the process amid ongoing tensions between the Trump administration and ABC late-night host Jimmy Kimmel.

The eight stations must demonstrate they have been operating in the public interest as part of an ongoing look at Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) practices. While the FCC filing did not specifically mention Kimmel, ABC argues the action is retaliatory.

CONSERVATIVE GROUPS URGE FCC TO BACK OFF ABC LICENSE REVIEW, WARNING IT COULD HURT RIGHT-LEANING MEDIA

"There is no question why the Commission is singling out these eight stations: Each is owned by ABC, and the Administration has openly and repeatedly called for the revocation of ABC’s licenses, because it dislikes the content and viewpoints expressed on ABC network programs," ABC’s legal team wrote.

KFSN-TV in Fresno; KABC-TV in Los Angeles; KGO-TV in San Francisco; WLS-TV in Chicago; WABC-TV in New York; WTVD in Durham, N.C.; WPVI-TV in Philadelphia; and KTRK-TV in Houston are the Disney-owned stations in question.

"The outpouring of support for the Stations has been unprecedented for a license renewal proceeding," ABC wrote.

CONSERVATIVE WATCHDOG TELLS FCC THAT 'THE VIEW' IS A DEMOCRATIC PARTY OPERATION, NOT A NEWS PROGRAM

"Over 140,000 comments have been received from the Stations’ local communities — from individual viewers to local police and firefighters, charities, businesses, and schools — and over 95% support the Stations," the filing continued. "These supporters span the ideological spectrum but share a fundamental commitment to free speech and press freedom. This record demonstrates that the Stations serve the public interest with distinction."

ABC insists the FCC "has spent the last 18 months searching for some pretext for revoking the Stations’ licenses," but "has found none, because the Stations easily meet the standard for license renewal — which under the law means that the Commission cannot revoke their licenses or order a hearing on their renewal applications."

The Trump administration has had a beef with Kimmel, who lampoons the president on a regular basis and whose controversial "expectant widow" joke earlier this year resulted in first lady Melania Trump calling for him to be fired. The FCC has also launched a probe into ABC daytime show "The View," and Carr recently took exception to the Disney-owned network declining to air Trump’s primetime address on linear television.

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

"The retaliation against ABC is a signal to every media company in the country: accommodate the Administration’s view of what news coverage should look like or pay the price. Across the government, regulatory and contracting carrots and sticks have been trained on other disfavored speakers. The tools vary; the objective does not: a media industry too fearful of official reprisal to report the news freely," ABC wrote.

"Calling up the license of a single Station — let alone all eight at once — while the Commission’s DEI investigation has found no violation is unnecessary, premature, and punitive," ABC continued in the filing. "Even if any violation were ever substantiated, the Commission has a graduated set of well-established remedies far short of the corporate death penalty of license non-renewal."

An FCC spokesperson issued the following statement: "For decades, Americans of all stripes have been subsidizing broadcast media to the tune of many billions of dollars by giving TV stations free use of a valuable, public resource — the airwaves. In exchange, broadcasters are required by law to operate in the public interest, not in the narrow or partisan interests of a political party. 

"Broadcasters know that they are prohibited from engaging in invidious forms of DEI discrimination, that they must comply with political equal opportunity regulations and that they are barred from running broadcast hoaxes or distorting the news. The FCC is going to hold broadcasters accountable to the full extent of the law, regardless of any disinformation campaign that some of them may choose to run."

The Media Research Center (MRC), the conservative watchdog group that previously filed a petition in support of the early review of ABC's broadcasting licenses, doubled down on its stance.

"ABC's defense boils down to this: 'Trust us.' Americans do not, which is why confidence in the media is at historic lows," MRC President David Bozell told Fox News Digital. 

"Our filing is not based on hurt feelings or political disagreement. It is based on documented conduct. We look forward to the FCC reviewing the facts rather than the distractions."

item.title: If you believe Alabama wasn't recruiting Jeremiah Smith, you don't understand recruiting
item.description: Jeremiah Smith claimed Alabama wasn't recruiting him, but evidence shows Nick Saban offered him in 2022 after an unofficial visit to Tuscaloosa.
item.content:encoded:
College football recruiting has gone from a niche subset of the sport to something that has taken on a life of its own.

Just a few short decades ago, if you wanted to follow recruiting you almost had to seek it out, ordering magazine subscriptions and hanging out on message boards to stay on top of the latest rumors.

Now, fans can be inundated with recruiting news and factoids just by hanging out on social media, to the point where you're almost beaten over the head with it on a near daily basis.

FORMER OHIO STATE, FLORIDA COACH URBAN MEYER REVEALS THE ONE PLACE HE REFUSED TO RECRUIT PLAYERS FROM

Since recruiting has become more accessible to the layman, more and more fans have been able to fire off takes about the once-underground aspect of college football, and with that, we also see that plenty of fans still have a lot to learn about the inner workings of it all.

Take this latest revelation, for example.

Ohio State wide receiver and former five-star prospect Jeremiah Smith recently revealed to folks at Big Ten Media Days that Alabama was his dream school growing up, but he didn't end up going there because, for whatever reason, they failed to recruit him.

NICK SABAN URGES SENATE TO PASS LEGISLATION TO FIX COLLEGE SPORTS, BUT COACHING CONTRACTS GLOSSED OVER

I couldn't have rolled my eyes any harder upon hearing this, but after perusing the comments section and scrolling through various social media platforms, I was shocked to see the majority of people actually believed what Smith was feeding them.

I'm going to say this up front, as clearly as I can: if you actually think the Alabama Crimson Tide weren't recruiting Jeremiah Smith, then you have a fundamental misunderstanding of recruiting.

Allow me to break it down for you.

ED ORGERON-LANE KIFFIN PAIRING ALREADY PAYING DIVIDENDS FOR LSU TIGERS DURING PIVOTAL RECRUITING WEEKEND

Jeremiah Smith wasn't just an elite, five-star player. He was the number one player in his entire recruiting class of 2024.

The kid started receiving offers from Power 4 schools in February 2021, when he was going into his freshman year of high school.

I say all that to paint the picture that this isn't some three-star safety from Iowa who grew up dreaming of playing for USC and got looked over for whatever reason.

Smith was elite from day one, forged in the crucible of South Florida high school football.

Speaking of offers from Power 4 schools, it looks like Smith got one from none other than Nick Saban and Alabama all the way back in February 2022, less than one month after he took an unofficial visit to Bama.

That doesn't sound like a guy who "wasn't being recruited by a school" to me.

I've seen some people float the theory that Saban knew he was leaving after the end of the 2023 season and so he might have checked out on recruiting, but that doesn't match up at all with what Bama's 2024 class shows us.

The Crimson Tide signed the 2nd ranked recruiting class in the country in 2024, and even landed a couple of four-star prospects from the Sunshine State, so it's not like they completely neglected Smith's home state of Florida that cycle either.

Either Smith is trolling Alabama fans - and he has been known to rile up opposing fanbases in the past (see: Miami) - or he's not telling the whole truth, and I'm inclined to think it's more of the latter than the former.

Alabama and Nick Saban ABSOLUTELY recruited Jeremiah Smith to come to Tuscaloosa.

Who wouldn't want the best player in the country to wear their uniform in college?

But I also don't think Saban recruited him quite as hard as some of the other programs that were in his final list of schools.

To recruit a five-star is to practically get down on your knees and beg them to come to your school, and I just don't believe Saban was willing to go to the lengths others were willing to.

That's not to suggest Ohio State or any of Smith's other finalists did anything nefarious. Hell, it's practically impossible to do something illegal in today's day and age of recruiting.

It's likely the Buckeyes just "wanted him more."

Besides, the Tide had a five-star wide receiver of their own in Ryan Williams, so I doubt they were willing to "break the bank" for two of the top five wideout prospects in the same class.

That just doesn't sound like something out of Saban's playbook, but I could be wrong.

All of that is to say, Alabama almost certainly "recruited" Jeremiah Smith, as did every other program and coach with a pulse in America back in 2023.

It seems like they just didn't recruit him to a level of his liking.

Which is fine, that's his prerogative, but I disagree with Smith saying that Bama flat out wasn't pursuing him.

That's simply not true, but recruiting involves the whims of 17-year-old super athletes, so perception is often reality in their minds.

I've said it before and I'll say it again: big boy recruiting is not for the faint of heart, and the Jeremiah Smith saga is just the latest example of this.

item.title: Packers great running back Ahman Green reveals early-onset Parkinson's diagnosis
item.description: Ahman Green revealed his early-onset Parkinson's diagnosis on a podcast, detailing symptoms his wife first noticed after his NFL retirement in 2009.
item.content:encoded:
Former Green Bay Packers running back Ahman Green, who made four Pro Bowls with the franchise during his eight-year stint, has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.

Green made the announcement on the "Go Long" podcast with Tyler Dunne, saying he found out about his diagnosis last year.

"I got diagnosed with early-onset Parkinson’s," Green said. "I had a little bit of the feet twitching when I’m in my sleep and stuff like that.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I knew something was going on long before that. I just got a hold of some doctors that I was about to get in contact with. Get the diagnostics, get the testing. And finally got it tested last — it was January of 2025."

Green had kept his diagnosis close to the vest, with only his closest friends and family knowing for more than a year and a half. He said he didn’t want to share it for a long time, only telling his kids and close family. Now, he’s ready to share how he’s attacking it.

CARLY SIMON REVEALS THE COMMON CONDITION THAT MASKED HER PARKINSON'S DIAGNOSIS

"It needs to be up front. It needs to be a topic that’s always hit. And it’s not the end all," Green added.

"To me, I have a jump ahead of it. Just like anybody discovering that they have some type of cancer in their body, I’m ahead of it right now."

Green has been focused on eating healthy, making sure to exercise and taking his medication religiously.

The twitching while sleeping is something Green revealed his wife told him about after he retired in 2009 from the league. He’s now dealing with short-term memory loss as well as sleep walking and talking.

Green, though, remains optimistic and wants to be an advocate now for those going through a similar situation as him.

The Nebraska product began his NFL career as a third-round pick of the Seattle Seahawks, but he became a star at Lambeau Field after being traded to the Packers before the 2000 season.

Green immediately broke out with the Packers, tallying 1,175 rushing yards and 10 rushing touchdowns on 263 carries in his first season. He cemented himself as the bell cow back, and he earned four straight Pro Bowls from 2001-04.

His best season came in 2003, when he rushed for 1,883 yards and caught 50 passes for 367 yards with 20 total touchdowns on the year. Green finished his Packers career with 8,322 rushing yards and 54 rushing scores across 104 games.

Green also played two seasons for the Houston Texans before returning to the Packers in 2009, where he played in a reserve role in eight games.

item.title: James Talarico doesn't drive his own truck in viral Texas campaign ad featuring Dodge Ram
item.description: James Talarico’s campaign confirmed Thursday that the truck he’s driving in a viral advertisement doesn’t belong to the Democratic Texas Senate candidate.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico’s campaign confirmed Thursday that the truck he drove in a viral advertisement doesn’t belong to him. 

Talarico has previously revealed that he owns a midsize Chevy Colorado, but in a new campaign ad he is driving a full-sized Dodge Ram 1500. As a result of the vehicle swap, Talarico has been mocked by conservatives for appearing in the larger truck for the slick campaign commercial. 

Critics have accused Talarico of trying to "look like a real Texan," but his campaign said the switch was simply for production purposes. 

"James’ truck has tinted windows. We tried to shoot in his Chevy first, but it was too dark to film," Talarico campaign spokesperson JT Ennis told Fox News Digital.

CONSERVATIVES MOCK TALARICO FOR GUSHING OVER FAUCI DOLL IN RESURFACED CHRISTMAS POST

The ad, "Waking Up," essentially stars the Dodge Ram as Talarico drives through the Lone Star State while a voiceover features the Senate candidate discussing plans to "make this economy work for working people again." Throughout the video, shots of Talarico driving the dark Dodge Ram are intertwined with images of hardworking Texans.  

Semafor political reporter David Weigel noticed the "odd detail" in the ad. 

"He drives a Chevy Colorado, which has appeared in other ads and in profiles. But here he's driving a Dodge Ram 1500. And it's not hard to spot; you can see the plate, which is linked to an Enterprise rental," Weigel wrote. 

TEXAS DEM NOMINEE JAMES TALARICO INVOKES FAITH TO DEFEND ABORTION RIGHTS, ‘THE BIBLE IS SILENT ON ABORTION'

The Talarico campaign did not immediately respond when asked if the Dodge Ram was rented. 

Some truck enthusiasts have insisted that Talarico's Chevy Colorado is inferior. 

"You can look at the RAM and see it looks tougher than the Colorado. Size matters. That RAM is taller, longer, wider. More like a truck," conservative writer Caleb Howe wrote. 

Plenty took to X to mock Talarico:

Talarico is no stranger to criticism and was also lampooned on Thursday when it was revealed he celebrated receiving a Dr. Anthony Fauci doll in 2021. 

Republicans have sought to portray Talarico as effeminate in an effort to damage his image among Texas voters. Democrats haven't won a U.S. Senate race in the state since 1988.

Talarico's opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, branded Talarico as "too low-T for Texas." An AI ad produced by a conservative group portrayed the Democratic hopeful prancing around in a dress. 

TALARICO SAYS HE 'HATES CHRISTIANITY' IN UNEARTHED INTERVIEW WITH TRANSGENDER 'LATINX' THEOLOGIAN

Talarico's campaign took a shot at Paxton over his past legal troubles in its response to Fox News Digital, adding, "We look forward to seeing Ken Paxton's favorite ride — we hear it's the back of a police car."

Fox News Digital reached out to Paxton's campaign for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

Fox News Digital's Robert Schmad contributed to this report.

item.title: US Olympian Lolo Jones accuses USOPC, USA Bobsled for 'nearly paralyzing' her over mistreated injuries
item.description: Lolo Jones says the USOPC and USA Bobsled nearly paralyzed her by denying medical treatment for a broken back before the 2025 World Championships.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Olympian and world champion track star and bobsledder Lolo Jones says the United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee (USOPC) and USA Bobsled "risk[ed] permanent paralysis" after mistreating her serious back injuries, which she competed with.

Jones broke a year-plus hiatus on X to share a story from Zielhaus that she "couldn't talk about," which explained her injuries, lack of treatment and eventual suspension from the Olympic Training Center.

The piece said Jones broke her back during a "race-off for the USA 1 brakewoman seat" in Lake Placid, New York, "days before the 2025 World Championships." 

Jones suffered "brutal lower-back pain, numbness, leg instability, foot drop, loss of bladder control."

Jones then had a massage scheduled with the Olympic Training Center's trainer, but the appointment was "canceled" by John Faltus, a "top official at the USOPC medical clinic," because Jones was "only entitled to one massage per week and had already received one that week," the piece said.

item.title: Angry cruise passengers blast major line over surprise daily gratuity hike
item.description: Celebrity Cruises raised its automatic gratuity charges by $1.50 per person per day. Some angry passengers are threatening to remove their payment of the fees and tip in cash.
item.content:encoded:
Passengers of Celebrity Cruises are pushing back after the cruise line raised its automatic gratuity charges with little notice, with some guests threatening to remove their payment of the fees altogether and tip crew members in cash instead.

As of July 29, guests who do not prepay the gratuities will automatically pay between $19.50 and $24.50 per person, per day, depending on their stateroom category, according to the Celebrity Cruises gratuity policy on the company's website.

The increase raises the daily gratuity by $1.50 per person across every stateroom category, according to reports.

AMERICA’S TIPPING CULTURE HAS GONE FROM REWARDING SERVICE TO FEE INSANITY

Under the new rates, guests staying in Inside, Ocean View and Veranda staterooms will pay $19.50 per person, per day.

Concierge Class and AquaClass guests will pay $20.50, while those staying in The Retreat will pay $24.50, the policy states.

The gratuity program is part of crew compensation and reflects industry standards, while guests frequently credit crew members with making their vacations memorable, a spokesperson from Miami-based Royal Caribbean Group — of which Celebrity Cruises is part — told Fox News Digital.

The cruise line also automatically adds a 20% gratuity to purchases including beverages, beverage packages, specialty dining, room service, minibar items and spa and salon services, according to the policy.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

While many passengers said they support the idea of tipping crew members, they criticized the timing of the announcement, saying they were notified on the same day the higher rates took effect.

"Today is July 29. Nice bit of lead time," one Reddit user wrote about what happened. "I might have paid in advance for the savings... but this sucks."

"Not 'We're raising gratuities in a week, you can pay the current rate until then.' It's RIGHT NOW," another user wrote.

Several passengers said the cruise line should simply build gratuities into the advertised fare, rather than charging them separately.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"At this point, they just need to include gratuities in their fare like the luxury lines do," one Reddit user wrote.

Several guests said they planned to opt out of the automatic gratuities and instead hand cash directly to crew members, saying they wanted to ensure the money reached the employees who served them.

"I've started removing them and spending the exact same amount or more in direct tips," one passenger wrote. 

"At least then I know what I'm paying is going directly to the workers."

Not all reactions were negative, however.

"My stateroom attendants have always been great. I don't mind the gratuity going up," one Reddit user wrote. 

"Celebrity could have rolled this out more thoughtfully, though."

item.title: World Series champion Joe Giradi reveals the two major things impacting the trade deadline
item.description: World Series champion Joe Girardi talked to Fox News Digital about the impact the additional postseason spots and the expiration of the CBA will have on the MLB trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
One of the busiest and most exciting times of Major League Baseball’s season is rapidly approaching: the trade deadline.

This year’s trade deadline is set for Aug. 3 at 6 p.m. ET with plenty of contenders looking to bolster their rosters. However, looming over the trade deadline is the expiration of the CBA and the lack of sellers.

In 2022, Major League Baseball added the third wild-card spot to the postseason, allowing more teams to remain in contention. At the time of this writing, all but seven teams are within 5½ games of the final wild-card spot, making more teams reluctant to part ways with key pieces while chasing a playoff berth.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

World Series champion Joe Girardi said the sellers will control the market.

"Well, I think it changes it completely because so many teams are still in it," Girardi told Fox News Digital in a recent interview. "I would say there's only probably seven teams that would consider themselves eliminated out of the 30 so far. 

"So, that means there's probably not going to be a lot of people traded from the other 23 teams. So, everyone's going to be in the hunt for those guys on those seven teams. And there's only so many that you can acquire."

The Cincinnati Reds, New York Mets, San Francisco Giants, Colorado Rockies, Los Angeles Angels, the Athletics and Kansas City Royals are expected to be among the sellers.

"I think it's going to make it really interesting. I think for the seven teams that are probably planning on moving players at this time, I think they're in a great position to rebuild because their assets are going to become, teams are going to come at him hard, and you're going to get some pretty good deals."

Girardi, who won three World Series as a player during his 15-year career and one as a manager of the New York Yankees, said the expiration of the CBA will change how teams operate.

JOE GIRARDI, SHANE VICTORINO TO MANAGE TOP HIGH SCHOOL BASEBALL TALENT AT PERFECT GAME ALL-AMERICAN CLASSIC

While Girardi remains confident Major League Baseball and the MLB Players Association will strike a deal, he expects teams to be more aggressive.

"I think they will. I think teams will go for it more in a sense, not knowing what's going to happen next year. And I'm still a strong believer that a deal will get done. Because it always does. There's nothing in the history of the game that tells me that either side is willing to shut it down for a whole year," Girardi told Fox News Digital on behalf of Perfect Game.

"But there's always that risk, and sometimes teams get older, they figure that their window is closing. Let's go for it now because we don't know what's going to happen next year, and we'll just adjust when we have to."

The Los Angeles Dodgers are going for their third straight World Series championship this season, and two-time reigning Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal could be on the move as the Detroit Tigers continue to scuffle, according to ESPN. 

The Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays are all expected to be in on Skubal, according to the report.

San Diego Padres All-Star closer Mason Miller could be on the move, but the team is just 1½ games behind the race for a wild-card spot in the National League.

If some of the teams within striking distance of the final wild-card spot — like the Baltimore Orioles (2½ games back), Tigers (4½ games back), Miami Marlins (2 games back), Washington Nationals (2 games back) and St. Louis Cardinals (2½ games back) — decide to blow it up, they could change the landscape of the sport.

Girardi was a catcher in the big leagues for 15 years. He spent the first four seasons of his career with the Chicago Cubs, the next three with the Rockies, the next four with the Yankees and returned to the Cubs for three years before spending his final season with the Cardinals. He made the All-Star Game in 2000 with the Cubs.

He had a career .267 batting average with 36 home runs and 424 RBI. After his playing career, he became a manager. He spent one season with the Marlins in 2006 and then managed the Yankees for 10 seasons, beginning in 2008. Girardi most recently managed the Phillies for 2½ years from 2020 to 2022.

item.title: 'Disrespected' Baker Mayfield warns Buccaneers 'it's only going to get worse' after failed contract talks
item.description: Baker Mayfield says he feels "disrespected" and "undervalued" by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after contract negotiations ended without a long-term deal.
item.content:encoded:
Baker Mayfield used the word "disrespected" and phrases such as "very disappointed to say the least" and "undervalued after thinking you've earned it," so it's pretty obvious the team's starting quarterback is not thrilled about how the Tampa Bay Buccaneers handled his recent contract negotiations.

Those negotiations have ended now. Mayfield imposed a start-of-training-camp deadline to bring them to a close and he's sticking to it.

But the weeks of negotiations and offers the Bucs made before the deadline have left him in an unhappy place. And that's not a good place for any player, much less the team's starting quarterback, to be to start training camp.

BAKER MAYFIELD'S SELF-IMPOSED CONTRACT DEADLINE ARRIVES AS BUCCANEERS AND QUARTERBACK FAIL TO AGREE ON DEAL

"It's disappointing in the regard to have, you know, to feel disrespected a little bit," Mayfield told reporters. "And, um, that's really the disappointing part to feel undervalued after, you know, thinking you've earned it.

"This is not a poor-me thing. There's a lot other people that have it way worse off, but I can sit here and look at other quarterbacks and peers and evaluate myself based on that and put myself in certain categories that I deserve to be compensated for that.

"And I think I'm a franchise quarterback. I've been told I'm a franchise quarterback. It's been said publicly from ownership down here. And so to not have a deal done is very disappointing."

Mayfield told ESPN the Bucs didn't offer anything beyond a two-year deal. He actually wanted a longer-term deal that would have kept him in Tampa into his mid-30s.

There are currently 10 NFL quarterbacks who make between $51 million and $55 million per season on an annual average basis. Mayfield wants to be part of that group.

Mayfield instead will collect up to $28 million in the final year of his three-year deal that averaged $33.3 million per season.

The quarterback and the team have agreed not to discuss the contract situation again this season, in part, because of Mayfield's deadline. But anyone who knows Mayfield knows him not talking about it and not thinking about it are two different things.

He's going to think about how he feels he's been treated.

"It's disappointing when you think you're the cornerstone of the franchise to be treated like that," he admitted.

He's going to feel free to take shots at the club if he feels the need. He did exactly that on Thursday, criticizing how the Bucs have historically handled negotiations with other players including Mike Evans and Tristan Wirfs, and are currently dealing with Vita Vea, who has requested a trade.

And Mayfield is going to use all that as fuel and motivation to have an outstanding year. If he has that kind of season, he's obviously going to command more than what he was expecting in the just concluded negotiations.

"If you waited this long to take care of your franchise quarterback, that's too bad because it's only going to get worse from here," he said, as if announcing to the team what would happen in future talks.

Mayfield addressed his teammates about his contract talks. Yeah, this is a locker room issue now even as Mayfield promised he's done talking about money.

"I addressed the team to let them know ... It's all ball with these guys," he vowed. "I think all the guys that have been here know exactly who I am. The guys that haven't been here I wanted to address that because they might have had a notion prior to coming here about who I am as a person.

"But it's all team. It's all about winning here now and what we're going to do."

Mayfield loves Tampa. He has said numerous times he'd love to raise his family there.

It doesn't escape scrutiny in the context of his current feelings and contract situation that on Thursday he called it, "home for now."
