item.title: Trump administration probes Minnesota over 'transgender dolls' in schools, but state disputes story
item.description: The Trump administration launched a federal probe into Minnesota's use of "MyGender Dolls" in classrooms, but Tim Walz's office says no such program is being implemented.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration is threatening to strip federal funding from the Minnesota Department of Education (MDE) as part of a federal investigation into reports that "transgender dolls" are being introduced in classrooms, although the state claims it has no involvement and no such program is happening.

A Department of Education (ED) official told Fox News Digital that the probe was opened by the agency's Student Privacy Policy Office following a privacy complaint filed by the advocacy group Defending Education. The complaint alleged that Minnesota parents were not notified — nor given the opportunity to opt their children out — of classroom activities involving "MyGender Dolls."

If the federal probe finds that state officials violated the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA) or infringed upon parental rights, the state risks losing key federal education dollars.

TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS WOKE SCHOOLS ACCUSED OF HIDING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS

The Minnesota Department of Education said, however, it "has no involvement" with the program and pointed to the University of Minnesota housing a study on the dolls.

"This is a University of Minnesota study/program. The Minnesota Department of Education has no involvement with this," a spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

Developed through a program housed at the University of Minnesota, "MyGender Dolls" feature paper characters with removable and interchangeable internal and external genitalia, clothing, and accessories designed for children as young as 4 years old.

"If we are able to determine that the Minnesota Department of Education has violated federal parental rights laws, this could include referral to the Department of Justice, and violation of those laws could result in the termination of the Minnesota Department of Education's federal funding," ED spokesperson Amelia Joy told Fox News Digital.

In response to the backlash, researchers behind the project stated that the dolls are intended as "a therapeutic tool for use by licensed professionals" and said the dolls will not be distributed in public school classrooms this fall.

TRUMP ADMIN PAUSING OVER $1B IN MEDICAID PAYMENTS TO MINNESOTA, CALIFORNIA OVER FRAUD, COMPLIANCE CONCERNS

Joy said that the dolls were "shocking."

"I'd like to take a moment to point out the fact that these dolls, in this case in Minnesota, the MyGender Dolls, were advertised for use in classrooms with students as young as four years old," Joy said. "They were actually developed through a taxpayer-funded program at the University of Minnesota. So, Governor Walz is using taxpayer dollars to create these dolls for 4-year-olds so that they can play with representations of genitalia that are removable and interchangeable."

However, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz's office disputes Joy's claims that the dolls were facilitated through a "taxpayer-funded" effort, saying the program was created through private donors and is supported entirely by a privately funded grant. 

"The Governor has no connection to this program. It was not developed or funded by the Minnesota Department of Education and is not being implemented in Minnesota schools under the Walz Administration. This entire story has been manufactured by right-wing media to distract from President Trump's flailing economy and never-ending war," the governor's office told Fox News Digital.

University of Minnesota officials doubled down on rejecting such sentiments.

"The University of Minnesota is firmly committed to supporting the innovative research of our faculty and students," a spokesperson from the university told Fox News Digital.

The statement added: "The team that developed MyGender Dolls participated in privately funded review competitions and received no state or federal dollars to support the development of the dolls or commercialization efforts. MyGender Dolls is a private, independent LLC, not affiliated with the University of Minnesota."

In a press release, ED officials described the dolls as "sexually explicit" and argued that using them with young children undermines parental authority over sensitive subjects. Under the PPRA, parents hold the explicit statutory right to review instructional materials and opt their children out of surveys or activities involving sensitive personal topics.

"While Governor Walz and the radical left continue to funnel taxpayer dollars to perverted ideologies that can harm children, the Trump Administration is fighting to protect children’s innocence and defend parents’ role as the first and primary decision-makers in their child’s education," U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon said in a statement. "No four-year-old should be exposed to such material – especially without a parent’s knowledge or consent. ED will enforce the law to its fullest extent, putting parents and families firmly in the driver’s seat of their child’s education."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION OPENS FOUR TITLE IX INVESTIGATIONS INTO MICHIGAN AND NORTH CAROLINA SCHOOL DISTRICTS

The action against Minnesota comes as the Trump administration expands a broader campaign against gender-identity policies in public schools. On Monday — National Parents Day — the Department of Education partnered with the DOJ to take enforcement action against two other school districts accused of violating the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA).

Federal officials warned Anne Arundel County Public Schools in Maryland and Ann Arbor Public Schools in Michigan that they could lose federal funds for allegedly concealing information from parents regarding their children's gender transitions at school.

item.description: A babysitter's confession, a 43-year age gap hookup at a Waco pool, and Justin Herbert and Madison Beer's engagement highlight this week's romance roundup.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a long week, but not long enough too keep me from filing another True Romance. I always have the energy, even if some weeks require more coffee than others, for our weekly strolls through the sometimes complicated world of romance.

If a 67-year-old on Tinder has enough energy to look for a sugar baby and to get arrested on charges related to allegedly getting upset when his date called her friends to pick her up, I should be able to sit down and handle my responsibilities.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

We have a 75-year-old getting busted for allegedly getting on with a 32-year-old woman at an apartment complex pool over the weekend to thank for that knowledge. That's not the only lesson these two have for us this week.

It turns out this week is full of lessons. From poolside hookups to the magic of shooting your shot with your crush, there's a lot to learn. We're going to get started with the confession of a babysitter.

The lesson here is to always pay the babysitter, especially when your husband is always on business trips, and you're fooling around behind his back. Paying what you owe is the least you can do.

I can't get started without mentioning the biggest offseason love story in the NFL. No, not the Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce story. I still say if they don't have any children that it was all a show.

I'm talking about the engagement of Justin Herbert and Madison Beer, of course. Congratulations to the two of them. That's a real love story.

Go follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook. Send your emails here: sean.joseph@outkick.com (anonymously if you prefer).

I suppose the easiest solution to not getting caught cheating would be to not cheat in the first place. Since that's out of the question for some, another approach might be to make sure that you stay on the good side of any witnesses to your infidelities.

Let's say you have a babysitter, for instance, who watches the kids while you're out running around behind your husband's back. The very least you could do is pay her more when you run late. I'd toss a healthy tip on top of that, but you play with as much fire as you want.

Because that's exactly what you're doing by coming home late and not paying them what you owe. The babysitter can ruin your "having cake and eating it too" situation at any time.

This confession from a babysitter who did just that should serve as a lesson to those of you who think the babysitter isn't going to say anything and that you can keep ignoring the fact that you're shorting them.

"I used to babysit for a couple whose husband was always away on business trips. The wife was cheating and constantly came home late, completely ignoring my extra hours and refusing to pay me," the babysitter wrote on Reddit.

"The final straw was when she was three hours late and stiffed me on the spot again. The very next time her side guy came over, I snapped a clear picture of them together."

See. This is exactly why you don't play around with witnesses. You either have none or take care of the ones who you do have. The babysitter took that picture and fired off a marriage ending text to her husband.

The text message read, "Since I'm not getting paid, thought you should see what she's busy doing."

All that had to be done was to pay for the extra time the babysitter spent at your house watching your kids while your husband was out of town. That's it. Since that's the approach that was taken, other methods were used.

"Their marriage ended shortly after, and I consider my debt fully settled," added the babysitter.

Let me say this before I get emails falsely claiming this babysitter is anti-romance. I'd say that was the case if she was fully compensated for her time and started making demands for her silence.

I don’t see any indication of that whatsoever.

It appears to me, she was more than willing to mind her own business and leave romance in the hands of those pursuing it.

The wife got too caught up in the pursuit and didn’t take time to make sure everything was handled properly. It cost her marriage, but let’s hope it didn’t cost her a shot at love.

Follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook.

Now to Waco, Texas, where police arrested a 75-year-old man and a 32-year-old woman on charges of public lewdness, reports KWTX.

These two, like the cheating wife stiffing her babysitter, got too caught up in the pursuit of romance, allegedly. It took place at an apartment complex pool around 5 p.m. on Sunday.

Officers were called to investigate reports of indecent exposure. Multiple witnesses had called alleging that the 43-year, age gap couple were having sex and there were children present.

The witnesses interviewed told officers that they were in the back corner of the pool and that the woman was allegedly on top of the man "grinding and thrusting" while moaning loudly.

The 75-year-old man admitted that the much younger woman was on top of him, but claimed they weren't having sex because he has a "penile implant." He did, however, admit that there was sexual contact.
